page: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Edsv7 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs derived from 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory capacity is 160.0 GB, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via an 1181 GB disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1983.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 35.47 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 20081.26 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12981.0.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a read-only small block cached speed of 1477.57 GB/sec, dropping to 141.96 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while large block write bandwidth is 58.49 GB/sec. Database operations are supported by a Passmark database score of 10336.74 and Redis SET operations performing at 34.81 million operations per second. For AI workloads, the server processes 135M model prompts at 2009.7 tokens per second and 7B model prompts at 124.5 tokens per second, though it lacks GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is suitable for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, and caching layers.
